member.name: T:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController
member.summary: Runs the device as an EtherNet/IP Scanner (the client/originator side — the role that talks to PLCs, motor drives, or other EIP adapters). Pure C# implementation, no native interop.

remarks.para: Property-bag API: configure the connection by setting properties (, , , , , etc.) before calling . Changing properties after the connection is up has no effect on the live session.

Thread safety: is written by the receive thread while your application reads it (torn-read risk). New code should subscribe to instead, which delivers a race-free byte[] snapshot. is kept for backwards compatibility.

member.name: P:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.LastReceivedImplicitMessage
member.summary:
Returns the Date and Time when the last Implicit Message has been received fŕom The Target Device Could be used to determine a Timeout.
NOTE: this is a wall-clock timestamp (DateTime.Now) and breaks if the system clock jumps (NTP sync, DST, manual set). For timeout detection that must survive clock changes, read instead and compare against Environment.TickCount.

member.name: P:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.LastReceivedImplicitMessageTickCount
member.summary: Monotonic (clock-jump-safe) counterpart of . Stores Environment.TickCount at the moment the last Class-1 packet was received from the target. Compare against a fresh Environment.TickCount read to compute elapsed-since-last-implicit, e.g. (Environment.TickCount - scanner.LastReceivedImplicitMessageTickCount) > 5000 for a 5-second watchdog. Unlike , this value is not affected by NTP sync, DST changes, or manual clock adjustment.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.ListIdentity(GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.Devices.Network.NetworkController,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Broadcasts an EIP List Identity command and collects responses from every EtherNet/IP device on the local subnet during the timeout window.
member.param: The TinyCLR NetworkController whose IP/mask is used to compute the broadcast address.
How long to listen for responses. Spec says devices reply within a random 0–2 s delay window, so use ≥ 2 s for reliable discovery. Pass TimeSpan.Zero to wait indefinitely (not recommended).
member.returns: One per responding device, or null if no device responded.
member.remarks: Current implementation broadcasts to the directed subnet address (e.g. 192.168.1.255 for a /24). Devices behind a router won't see the request unless directed-broadcast forwarding is enabled.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.RegisterSession(System.UInt32,System.UInt16)
member.summary: Opens a TCP connection to the target on port 44818 (0xAF12) and sends an EIP RegisterSession command to establish an encapsulation session. Required before any explicit-messaging service (GetAttributeSingle, ForwardOpen, etc.) can be sent.
member.param: Target IP as a packed 32-bit value: top byte is the first IPv4 octet (e.g. 192.168.1.1 = 0xC0A80101). Use the string overload if you have a dotted-quad string.
TCP port — typically 0xAF12 (44818, EIP standard). Pass a non-standard port only if the target listens elsewhere.
member.returns: The 32-bit session handle assigned by the target. Stored internally; you typically don't need to inspect it.
member.remarks: This call blocks until the TCP connect succeeds, fails, or the OS-level timeout fires (typically 60–120 s for unreachable hosts). There is no per-call timeout knob — if you might point at unreachable IPs, run this on a thread you can abandon.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.UnRegisterSession
member.summary: Sends an EIP UnregisterSession command to gracefully close the encapsulation session, then closes the TCP connection. Idempotent — safe to call even if the target has already dropped. calls this for you.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.Dispose
member.summary: Tears down the scanner cleanly: closes the Class-1 connection (ForwardClose), unregisters the encapsulation session, closes all sockets. Each sub-step swallows its own exceptions so Dispose itself never throws (per the contract). Idempotent and safe to call from a using block on any code path including before .

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.ForwardOpen
member.summary: Opens a Class-1 (implicit / cyclic I/O) connection to the target using regular Forward Open (service 0x54). Configure all connection-related properties (, , , , , etc.) before calling.
member.remarks: Spawns two background threads — sendUDP producing O→T data at the negotiated RPI, and a receive loop that fires per T→O packet. Use Large Forward Open (the overload below) for connection sizes > ~500 bytes.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Scanner.ScannerController.ForwardOpen(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Opens a Class-1 implicit connection, choosing between regular Forward Open (service 0x54) and Large Forward Open (service 0x5B) based on the flag. Large form is required when either direction's payload exceeds ~500 bytes.
member.exception: Connection size exceeds buffer, missing configuration, etc. See exception message.
Target returned a CIP error status. Use data[42] + extended status to diagnose.
